classification.difficultyReason: Infers simple, double and triple zeroes from three graphs, then substitutes the y-intercept to determine the leading coefficient.

content.prompt: Each graph shows a cubic of the form $y=a(x-\alpha)(x-\beta)(x-\gamma)$ for some constant $a$ where $\alpha\leq\beta\leq\gamma$. Use the graph to determine these values and hence write down the equation of the cubic.

spec.description: Ungriddded cubic with roots −2, −1, 1, y-intercept 2, and arrowheads at both ends. The local maximum lies slightly right of the y-axis.
spec.mathematics: The supplied curve is y=−(x+2)(x+1)(x−1); its equation remains hidden from students.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible; equation and coefficients solution-only.

answer.worked:
The graph crosses at $-2$, $-1$ and $1$, so $\alpha=-2$, $\beta=-1$, $\gamma=1$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=a(x+2)(x+1)(x-1)\\2&=a(2)(1)(-1)\\2&=-2a\\a&=-1\end{align*}$$
Thus $y=-(x+2)(x+1)(x-1)$.

spec.description: Ungriddded cubic crossing at −1, touching at 2, with local maximum and y-intercept 2 on the y-axis. Both curve ends have arrowheads.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible; equation and coefficients solution-only.

answer.worked:
The graph crosses at $-1$ and touches at $2$, giving the double zero $2$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=a(x+1)(x-2)^2\\2&=a(1)(-2)^2\\2&=4a\\a&=\tfrac12\end{align*}$$
Thus $\alpha=-1$, $\beta=\gamma=2$ and $y=\frac12(x+1)(x-2)^2$.

spec.description: Ungriddded increasing cubic with y-intercept −2 and stationary crossing at x=2. Both curve ends have arrowheads.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible; equation and coefficients solution-only.

answer.worked:
The horizontal crossing at $2$ gives a triple zero, so $\alpha=\beta=\gamma=2$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=a(x-2)^3\\-2&=a(-2)^3\\-2&=-8a\\a&=\tfrac14\end{align*}$$
Thus $y=\frac14(x-2)^3$.
